Paragraph:
Translation: Those who are seers of the truth have concluded that of the nonexistent there is no endurance, and of the existent there is no cessation. This seers have concluded by studying the nature of both.

Purport (Excerpt): There is no endurance of the changing body... But the spirit soul exists permanently, remaining the same despite all changes of the body and the mind. That is the difference between matter and spirit. By nature, the body is ever changing, and the soul is eternal.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna is struggling to reconcile the reality of the physical world (which is dying) with the concept of the eternal soul.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna introduces a binary framework of reality: the 'existent' (Sat - the eternal soul) and the 'nonexistent' (Asat - the temporary material body). He establishes that true knowledge requires seeing that the physical body has no permanent reality, while the soul never ceases to be.
Outcome/Resolution: This provides a philosophical foundation for detachment. If the body is fundamentally 'nonexistent' (because it is temporary), grieving its loss is irrational.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.reality Testing: Evaluating what is actually permanent vs. temporary
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.detachment: Letting go of attachment to transient forms

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sat (Truth, the eternal, that which exists permanently)
Asat (Untruth, the temporary, that which has no permanent existence)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The verse draws a definitive line between matter (asat) and spirit (sat). The material body is in a constant state of flux and ultimate destruction, therefore it has no absolute reality. The soul is unchanging and eternal, representing the only true reality. Realizing this removes the illusion that causes grief.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is a radical form of cognitive restructuring. Krishna is asking Arjuna to fundamentally alter his perception of reality. By classifying the physical body (and the impending deaths) as 'nonexistent' in a philosophical sense (because they are temporary), it reduces the cognitive weight and terror of the event. It trains the mind to focus only on what is permanent.
